headline.en: A round is one tune that fits itself when it starts at different times. You start it.

detail.en: Twice through, at an easy volume
Each one two bars behind the last
You'll hear the voices join as you sing

text.en: The first two lines, at your own pace.
After a bar of the drone, sing it twice through. Keep your own line while the voices come in.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes on pitch. By the end of the course you'll write your own line against a melody.

headline.en: Your ear can follow two voices at once. Listen for which one moves.

detail.en: One high, one low, at the same time
The other holds still, or sings its own tune

title.en: Hear it as often as you like

detail.en: Then choose

text.en: Listen to each, as often as you like, then choose.

why.en: The high voice stayed on one note while the low one climbed underneath.
The low voice held one note, like a drone, while the high one stepped down.
The high voice held. Under it, the low one went up and came back.
The low voice held do while the high one climbed away from it.

prompt.en: Same tune, or a different one?

why.en: The low voice sang the same tune two beats later: a little round.

prompt.en: Same tune, or a different one?

why.en: The low voice sang its own, slower line. Two different tunes that fit: that's counterpoint.

measures.en: Your stars are for the rounds you heard right the first time.

headline.en: A note held under a moving tune is a pedal, after the organ's pedals that can hold a low note forever.

detail.en: Do, on "oo", easy and steady
Ode to Joy, leaning on your note
Four holds, a quick breath each time

text.en: The guide gives you do. Hold it four times while the tune moves above you.
Now be the floor on so, below your do. The same tune, a new pedal.

measures.en: Your stars are for how long and how steadily you held your note while the tune moved.

headline.en: A pattern sung over and over is an ostinato, Italian for "stubborn". Once you know it, it keeps itself going.

detail.en: Do ti do la: a darker colour you'll meet properly in unit 2
Four times through
Let it pass; keep your pattern

text.en: The pattern, at your own pace.
After a bar of the high line, sing the pattern four times, then hold the last note.

measures.en: Your stars are for your pattern's notes on pitch while the other line moved.

headline.en: Under a whole tune: a pattern first, then one long note.

detail.en: Two notes a bar, under the first half
A pedal under "merrily" to the end
Could you still hear the tune?

text.en: After a bar, sing do and so under the tune, then hold do to the end.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes on pitch, the long one too. Could you still hear the tune while you held the floor?

headline.en: Now you come in second. The leader is already singing other notes when you start.

detail.en: Are You Sleeping, from the top
On "Are you sleeping"
Even when theirs is louder in your ear

text.en: Your first two bars, at your own pace.
The guide leads. Come in two bars later and sing it through.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes on pitch while the leader sang other notes.

headline.en: Minor is the same tune with two notes a half step lower: mi and la. It sounds darker. Mahler turned this round into a slow march in minor in his First Symphony.

detail.en: The same shape, a darker colour
Two are singing before you come in
Listen for it against the others

text.en: The minor tune's first four bars, at your own pace.
Two voices start. Come in third, four bars in, and sing it through.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes on pitch, in minor, with two voices already going.

headline.en: A round is a canon that loops back to the start. A canon can begin at any distance or pitch: here, a bar behind and an octave away.

detail.en: The guide follows a bar later, an octave down
The guide leads, an octave up
Do re do la, so ti la do...

text.en: The canon's line, at your own pace.
You lead. After the guide's do, sing the line, then hold do while the follower finishes.
Now you follow. The guide leads an octave up; come in a bar later.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes on pitch as the follower, a bar behind the leader.

headline.en: The hardest seat in a round: two voices are already singing when you start, and one more comes in after you.

detail.en: Come in four bars in
Above you, below you, and after you
Hold it the way you held your pedal

text.en: Two voices start. Come in third, four bars in, and sing it through while the fourth joins you.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes on pitch with a voice on every side. Could you still hear the others while you sang?

headline.en: A phrase that ends away from do sounds like a question. The answer brings it home.

detail.en: A short phrase, ending away from do
A different phrase, landing on do
From West African singing into gospel, blues and work songs

text.en: Hear the call, then sing the answer: mi re do.
Four calls, each with its answer. Sing each answer right after its call.

measures.en: Your stars are for your answers' notes on pitch.

title.en: A slow line under a tune

headline.en: Your line keeps falling while the tune turns, so the two never move the same way for long.

detail.en: Do, ti, la, so
Its notes move four times faster
Where each of your notes begins

text.en: Your four notes, at your own pace.
The guide gives you do. Then sing your slow line under Ode to Joy.

measures.en: Your stars are for your slow line's notes on pitch while the tune moved above.

headline.en: A descant floats above the tune in longer notes, so the tune still comes through. Choirs save it for the last verse.

detail.en: O Come, All Ye Faithful
Five long notes on "ah"
Let the tune be heard through you

text.en: The descant, at your own pace.
After a bar, sing the descant over the tune.

measures.en: Your stars are for the descant's notes on pitch over the tune.

headline.en: Songs on the same chords fit together, whatever their tunes. Singing two at once is a quodlibet, Latin for "whatever you please".

detail.en: Twice through
Swung, so it fits bar for bar
Both rest on do

text.en: After a bar of the drone, sing Row, Row, Row twice through while the guide sings Are You Sleeping.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes on pitch while a different song went on above you.

headline.en: Sing the tune, then come back for the last verse with the descant above it.

detail.en: The tune itself
Your descant, floating above
Let the last note ring

text.en: Verse one: sing the tune.
The last verse: the descant above the tune, and hold the last note.

measures.en: Your stars are for the descant's notes on pitch and the last long note. Could you hear the tune under you?
